reel: Pushinka: the Soviet space dog's puppy Khrushchev gave the Kennedys (1961) and her four 'pupniks' (1963)
status: 11 files: 10 photos + 1 clip. 7 are US federal works (JFK Library / NARA White House photographs by Stoughton and Knudsen, USIS Vienna photo and USIA film) = public domain. 2 are Moscow city archive photos published by mos.ru under CC BY 4.0 (Commons {{Mos.ru|4}}). 2 are scans of Soviet official documents from the JFK Library's Pushinka folder (JBKOPP-SF050-014), kept under PD-RU-exempt (official documents of a state body) with a note. The JFK Library asset viewer is behind Cloudflare: the Drupal pages and download endpoints block curl, but the IIIF manifests (https://www.jfklibrary.org/iiif/<orangeDamSystemId>/manifest) and the static.jfklibrary.org originals do not, so the 3000-px originals were pulled from there. The faceted JFK Library search for 'Pushinka (Dog)' threw a Cloudflare human-verification challenge, which was NOT bypassed; so the photo list below is what Commons/DPLA, the known folder IDs and the JFK Library's own pets page expose. No colour photo of Pushinka on the slide was found. The USIA film is sepia-toned colour, 253 s; transcoded from the Commons .ogv to H.264 mp4 (derived file).

assets.license: Public domain (US federal government work). JFK Library record: Copyright Status 'Public Domain', Use Restriction 'Unrestricted'. Accession ST-C235-3-63, 1 negative (color; 35 mm).
assets.license_note: White House photograph by Cecil Stoughton, Office of the Military Aide. Pulled at original 3000 px from the Library's IIIF manifest (orangeDamSystemId JF1STO248922).
assets.credit_line: Cecil Stoughton. White House Photographs. John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum, Boston (ST-C235-3-63)
assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR. 9 July 1963, South Lawn: White House electrician and kennel keeper Traphes Bryant lies on the grass in a grey work shirt holding white Pushinka, who grins at the camera, with her four dark brown pupniks (Butterfly, White Tips, Blackie, Streaker) lined up in front of her. South Portico of the White House and a station wagon behind.
assets.best_segments: THE OPENER. Push in on Pushinka's face and the four pups (x 400-900, y 450-730 in a 1200-wide preview); 9:16 crop centred on the dog keeps Bryant's face above and the pups below. Second beat: tilt up to the South Portico to establish 'the White House'.

assets.license: PD-RU-exempt (official document of a Soviet state body: Kennel of the USSR Academy of Sciences, 'Dog Passport No. B-087', stamped and signed); scan by the JFK Library (US government, no new copyright).
assets.license_note: MODERATE RISK. The passport form, typed entries, stamp and signature are an administrative document and exempt from copyright under Russian Civil Code art. 1259(6). The small pasted photo of Pushinka inside it is a 1961 Soviet photograph of unknown authorship and is arguably still copyrighted; it occupies ~5% of the frame. Keep the shot on the typed right-hand page if you want zero risk.
assets.credit_line: Pushinka's dog passport, Kennel of the USSR Academy of Sciences, 1961. Jacqueline Bouvier Kennedy Onassis Personal Papers, JBKOPP-SF050-014, John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum
assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR scan of the open blue dog passport: left page a small B&W photo captioned 'ПУШИНКА'; right page typed in Russian: breed 'беспородная' (mixed breed), name 'Пушинка', female, born 30 November 1960, place of birth kennel of the USSR Academy of Sciences, white and fluffy with pale spots, 6 kg; father 'Пушок' b. 1955, participant in numerous ground experiments; mother 'Стрелка' b. 1958, participant in the space flight of 19-20 August 1960 on the second space ship-satellite; owner: kennel of the USSR Academy of Sciences, Moscow, Leninsky prospekt 14; purple round stamp and signature of the kennel head (Radkevich).
assets.best_segments: Slow pan down the right page; punch in on the 'Мать "Стрелка" ... 19-20 августа 1960' lines for the 'her mother flew in space' beat. Cover p0003 (passport cover 'Паспорт собаки № В-087') is also in the scratchpad if a title card is wanted.

assets.license: PD-RU-exempt (official letter of the Chairman of the USSR Council of Ministers to a head of state = official document of a state body); scan by the JFK Library.
assets.license_note: Low risk: Commons hosts many Soviet government letters under {{PD-RU-exempt}}; text, not a creative photo.
assets.credit_line: Letter from Nikita Khrushchev to President Kennedy, 15 June 1961 (Russian original). Jacqueline Bouvier Kennedy Onassis Personal Papers, JBKOPP-SF050-014-p0010, John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum
assets.what_it_shows: Typed Russian letter on cream paper with the USSR state seal embossed at top, handwritten date '15' June 1961, signed 'Н. Хрущев'. Paragraph 2 says that Nina Petrovna and he are pleased to fulfil Mrs Kennedy's request and send the family little 'Pushinka', a direct descendant of the famous space traveller 'Strelka' who flew on 19 August 1960 and returned safely to Earth. Paragraph 1 is about the model whaling ship made of walrus tusk and whalebone.
assets.best_segments: Punch in on the word "Пушинку" and "Стрелки" in paragraph 2 (middle of page, roughly y 47-57%); a slow drift down to the signature for the 'Khrushchev' beat.

assets.what_it_shows: US Army DD Form 793 Rabies Vaccination Certificate, dated 22 June 1962, Organization 'WRAIR - Vet. Div.', Location 'Forest Glen, Md.', Owner 'President John F. Kennedy', address 'White House', species canine, breed 'Russian', age 2, weight 15, name Pushinka, colour white, female, tag 10714, signed Carol Max Lang, D.V.M., 1/Lt., VC.
assets.best_segments: Native portrait; a quick punch on 'OWNER'S NAME President John F. Kennedy / OWNER'S ADDRESS White House' and 'BREED Russian' is the joke beat. Use it with the Walter Reed line (she really was handled by the Army's Walter Reed vets).

assets.what_it_shows: B&W, 22 June 1961 (the week Pushinka arrived): Welsh terrier Charlie (left, tongue out) and white fluffy Pushinka (right, one ear up) sit on leads on the South Lawn with the full South Portico of the White House behind them.
assets.best_segments: Two-shot for the 'she met Charlie' beat; 9:16 crop on Pushinka with the portico columns above her. The first-days-at-the-White-House shot.

assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR, 14 August 1963, Squaw Island, Hyannis Port: JFK (blue polo) and Jacqueline Kennedy (pink) on a blue chaise with John Jr. holding cocker spaniel Shannon and Mrs Kennedy holding two of Pushinka's dark pupniks; Caroline in green overalls hugs Charlie; German shepherd Clipper stands, wolfhound Wolf lies on the flagstones. Pushinka herself is not in frame.
assets.best_segments: Square frame; 9:16 crop on Jackie + the two pups in her lap + Caroline with Charlie (centre-right). Use for 'the whole family' / 'the pups kept two' beat. NB: the two pups shown are White Tips and Blackie era (mid-Aug 1963, after Butterfly and Streaker were given away).

assets.best_segments: Crop to the boy and the puppy (lower centre). Cute insert for the 'pupniks' beat.

assets.what_it_shows: USIA newsreel excerpt of the Vienna summit, 3-4 June 1961: Vienna streets and Stephansdom, Air Force One arrival, Kennedy and Khrushchev meeting the press outside the US embassy residence, the two seated in talks, Khrushchev's motorcade arrival, crowds, and JFK's televised report to the nation.
assets.best_segments: 95-110 s: JFK and Khrushchev standing side by side outside the residence with the press (best Khrushchev + Kennedy two-shot). 150-170 s: Khrushchev's arrival by car. 185-195 s: the two seated in the meeting room. 60-65 s: honour guard at the airport. Avoid 0-60 s and 225-253 s (JFK speaking to camera / London).
